title: Travels with Buddy Petit and his strokes
summary: They travelled to Chicago and Texas; Petit's first stroke affected his hand and mouth, the second killed him; Penn was with him about five years.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Where did you all go? On the long trips or just...?
Well, uh, we went to Chicago and, uh, went to Texas and all about different places. I was with him when he took the last stroke he died in a cupboard. That's the way he died.
What kind of stroke did he have? Was he paralyzed or anything? Paralyzed stroke. Really bad.

And it hit him so he couldn't talk. Oh. Couldn't move at all? Well, a very little bit he did before he died after the second stroke. Uh huh. How did the first stroke leave him? In what... Well, it just, it left his hand in bad shape and his mouth was twisted just a little bit on the first stroke he had. And then, uh, but my mother after that, well, he could play. But he couldn't play like he would like to play, but he could play a little bit.
Do you know how old he was? Was he much older than you? I know...
Well, he was around, he was around the same age me and him was. It was a buddy petite. Yes. When he, when he died. Uh huh.
How long were you with him all together about Sammy? How many years?
Well, I don't know exactly. Uh, I, I, to my remembrance I stayed with him about five years.
Uh huh. Well, how long, uh, how long had you been with him before he had his first stroke?
Oh, I had been with him. In fact, I played with the band about, about three years and something before he had a stroke, because we used to travel together.
Uh huh. And then, uh, he had another one about two years after that? That's right. Uh huh.
Well, he wasn't very old when he died then, was he?
No, he wasn't too old when he died, Mr. Bill. He was still in his, uh, nice, uh, prime to play music and he was, he was a real good musician.
